artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a prime p, let $\left(\frac{a}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol. Consider the following three statements concerning the Chudnovsky-type series associated with the Heegner number 163.

(i) For every prime $p > 5$ with $p \neq 23, 29$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \frac{\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}}{(-640320)^{3k}} \equiv \begin{cases} \left(\frac{-10005}{p}\right)(x^2 - 2p) \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } \left(\frac{p}{163}\right) = 1 \text{ and } 4p = x^2 + 163 y^2 \text{ with } x,y\in\mathbb{Z}, \\ 0 \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } \left(\frac{p}{163}\right) = -1. \end{cases}$$

(ii) For every prime $p > 5$ with $p \neq 23, 29$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \frac{545140134\, k + 13591409}{(-640320)^{3k}} \binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k} \equiv 13591409\, p \left(\frac{-10005}{p}\right) \pmod{p^3}.$$

(iii) For each integer $n \geq 2$, define
$$a_n \;=\; \frac{2n(2n+1)}{\binom{2n}{n}} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (545140134\, k + 13591409)\,(-640320^3)^{\,n-1-k}\,\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}.$$
Then $a_n \in \mathbb{Z}$ unless $2n+1$ is a power of 3, in which case $3 a_n \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus 3\mathbb{Z}$.

Prove or disprove each of (i), (ii), (iii).
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for proofs of this specific Chudnovsky-type supercongruence (involving the Heegner number 163 and the constants 545140134, 13591409, 640320) did not yield a published proof. Related Ramanujan-type supercongruence conjectures of Z.-W. Sun have been resolved in particular cases, but no source verifies the three statements together. The conjecture appears to remain open.
